title: St. Louis-Style Pork Strips with Tart Cherry Glaze
description: Lean pork sirloin takes on the sweet cherry and mild ancho flavors of the original ribs in a spoonable glaze.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: lean boneless pork sirloin
ingredients.note: Trim before weighing; choose an intact roast or chops.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve if visibly grainy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with cherry and oak, mixed in equal parts pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {paprika}, {ancho} and {garlic} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Shape the strips
steps.text: Slice {pork} across the grain into finger-length strips about 1/2 inch thick.

steps.title: Poach under cover
steps.text: Lower the strips into the smoked liquid in one layer, adding {topup} to just cover if needed. Fit the lid immediately. The cover replaces a stall wrap from the start.

steps.title: Check the center
steps.text: Cook covered at 275°F for about 10–22 minutes. Check early from the side of the thickest strips and remove from heat when each has reached 145°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered pork off heat for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Lift the strips
steps.text: Transfer the strips to a covered dish with a spoonful of broth.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Melt the cherry spread
steps.text: Stir {cherry} and {mustard} into the measured broth over medium heat until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Glaze the pork
steps.text: Turn the strips in the cherry glaze and divide the remaining glaze between both plates.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the sirloin the night before and keep it covered in the refrigerator. Option A uses cherry and ancho. For gentler Option B, replace the cherry spread with smooth pear puree, leave out the ancho and pass chile separately. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth.
